newsitem.title: UK: For someone who has everything - a coat of arms.
newsitem.headline: For someone who has everything - a coat of arms.

text.p: Burke's Peerage, the British publisher to the nobility, announced a new business project on Monday -- designing coats of arms, hitherto the symbol of "blue blood", for commoners.

The organisation, owners of titles such as Burke's Landed Gentry and Ruvigny's Titled Nobility of Europe, said anyone with 1,470 pounds ($2,360) to spare could apply for one, but not everyone would be accepted.
"Evidence of service to the community in particular, or a contribution to society in general, will be asked for," said publishing director Harold Brooks-Baker.
"We would also ask that applicants be able to trace their families back at least 100 years...it goes without saying that moral integrity in any candidate is essential."

He named German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, French President Jacques Chirac, U.S. President Bill Clinton, South African President Nelson Mandela and U.S. computer billionaire Bill Gates as people who would be offered the service.
A coat of arms has already been designed for Mandela by a team working under Peter Spurrier, who once held the traditional British title of Portcullis Pursuivant of Arms and York Herald.

It includes a red shield indicating vigour, a gold key representing freedom and liberation and a downward pointing sword symbolising authority, and is surmounted by a springbok, a deer after which South Africa's rugby team is named.
The motto below is "Freedom for All".
